releases.title: Underworld by Max Hillebrand
releases.summary: Fabian Sixsmith spends his nights in a government surveillance bunker hunting the Underworld’s most wanted cypherpunk, a blonde hacker known as T1n4Red. He thinks he has finally caught her in a few white pixels. But the people he’s trying to bring down may know far more about him than he realises.

releases.title: The Final Monopoly by Alexander Reeve
releases.summary: Congratulations, you won capitalism. You bought everything, and The Company is the only company. A narrator speaks directly to the man in the windowless office at the top, recounting how growth and efficiency devoured everything, step by step. It’s a chilling short fable in which the winner takes all, and then keeps going.

releases.title: The Last Node by Satillionaire
releases.summary: A father and his ten-year-old daughter hide in the ruins of a Mississippi boomtown, keeping a handmade bitcoin node alive on stolen sunlight and bike batteries. His late wife lives on as a hologram in his pendant. Each block they sign is an act of defiance, but tonight the other nodes on the network start disappearing, and a patrol drone is closing in.

releases.title: The Rainmaker by Joseph Sidari
releases.summary: In a desert future where California is underwater and Lake Mead is a puddle, rain is the world’s hottest commodity. A veteran broker working from the top of the Hoover Dam has a knee that aches before storms and whenever someone is trying to swindle her. Today, with no cloud in the sky, it’s killing her, and the buyer across the desk wants a lot of water at a very low price.

releases.title: Supplying the Slugs by TM de Saavedra
releases.summary: Semyon is a slick arms dealer in a space suit who has landed on a distant planet to introduce a village of fluorescent orange slugs to the joys of civilisation. He presents himself as a god, with a branded crate falling from the sky and a vintage Russian rifle. The slugs have their own opinions, and the sales pitch isn’t going according to plan.

releases.title: Beneath the Fall by SF
releases.summary: Rayleigh and Hiko wheel and deal in a post-collapse hellscape where fiat is toilet paper, the dealers want sats, and quintillion-dollar notes barely buy lunch. She’s hot-headed and he’s the cool diplomat, and the dealer’s warehouse is as grim as it gets. When he offers a “tour,” you know it’s not a good idea to say yes.

releases.title: The Vision Solution by Ninja Grandma
releases.summary: A stranger is tasered and arrested in a train station bathroom, but not before he presses a scrap of paper into your hand with twelve words written on it. With police drones overhead and AI reading every twitch of your body, the next steps are a risky game of acting calm. The paper may be worth a fortune or a death sentence.

releases.title: Fork War by Alex Gurevich
releases.summary: A thousand years from now, wars are fought over energy, quasars power the cryptominers, and the Cheerah-Weerah blockchain fork is tearing civilisations apart. Allison Lester lands her decommissioned warship on a remote fringe world with one goal: buy a hundred zeta-joules from a suspiciously well-dressed energy dealer. The price he quotes is an insult, and she’s about to find out why.

releases.title: Infinite Debt by Graeme Shimmin
releases.summary: Debt is hereditary, enforcement drones patrol the slums, and a lottery is the only hope of cancellation. Zarah, a collector’s agent, climbs forty-seven levels of a plastic-and-carbon tower to find a former debt-algorithm engineer who is now drowning in the very system she built. What Zarah offers could save them both, or cost them everything.

releases.title: The Fixer: Medical Device Exorcist by Eric Kay
releases.summary: In a future where corporations rent you your own heartbeat, a hacker nicknamed the Exorcist takes sat-sized jobs from desperate patients. Pacemakers die, eye implants lose their resolution, insulin pumps get paywalled, and he cracks them back to life, barely paying rent in turnips and onions. It’s a story about the people who fix what the corporations break.

releases.title: We Are Living Well by Anonymous
releases.summary: In a frozen, mud-brown land, a family of seed-pickers lives by a single slogan that the distant Gardeners keep chanting: we are living well. The family tells the story together, in alternating voices, through a bitter winter. Then one of them finds a strange clear stone in a shady clearing that shouldn’t exist, filled with seeds that shouldn’t be there.

releases.title: The Last Days by Mariska van der Merwe
releases.summary: In a quarantined city where a deadly virus has made everyone a threat, people queue at a checkpoint where a positive test can mean trade or execution. Akani waits in line with a stolen chip in his wrist, while a dictator on the giant hologram declares money worthless and survival the only currency. Every day is a gamble, and this one is about to cost more than he expected.

releases.title: Dreaming Big by Lindsay Burns
releases.summary: In a world where people sleep in bags, hammocks, and bunks, how well you dream decides your status. Jocelyn has just been promoted to the hammocks, where she hunts for treasure in vivid dreams to earn credits. The higher she climbs, the stranger the rules become, and she starts to wonder who is profiting from all that sleep.

releases.title: The Confisco by Luciano Rocha
releases.summary: Max wakes up hungover, opens his bank app, and sees millions in his account, nearly all of it blocked. After a baffling announcement from the economy minister, the street outside is filled with queues, riot police, and neighbours punching walls. It’s a fast, furious, and surprisingly funny look at what happens when the government decides your money isn’t yours.

releases.title: The Currency of a Childhood by Praise Samuel-Imaikop
releases.summary: In a neighbourhood of white picket fences, children wear leashes, parents need licences, and Sports Day is an investment audit. A child sits out the events, hungry and defiant, while grown-ups scout the field for a wonderful return on their money. Her silent rebellion against being a product is the start of something bigger.

releases.title: Daria’s Delightful Dancing Emporium by Jillian Godsil
releases.summary: Twenty years into Mars’s one-way colony called Joy, where the air is thin and everything is barcoded, a paper letter lands on Daria’s welcome mat. The repo-man is coming for her music centre. She teaches dance in a crumpled, rust-streaked studio, shares her home with an alien husband, and has run out of things the Corporation hasn’t already claimed.

releases.title: Proxy – Temet Nosce by Decent Money
releases.summary: Ada steps into her office elevator on an ordinary morning, and it stops between floors. A figure with no face pins her down, and when the lights return, her body and identity have been taken from her. She’s now a NoBody, wearing a smooth blank mask in a world that has stopped seeing her, and she has to find out who did it and why.

releases.title: Self-Immolation to Self-Custody by Will Schoellkopf
releases.summary: Nasser’s daughter is getting married on the beach in Beirut, and the bank won’t let him withdraw his own savings to pay for it. So he arrives with a pistol he has never fired, a can of petrol, and his ID. What happens next is a tense and darkly funny story about a desperate father and the money he can’t touch.

releases.title: Crushing by KT Morley
releases.summary: It’s bond auction day, and the diner’s crowd gets thinner every week. Marvin sips his coffee and warns the waitress to pull out her cash and stock up on food, gold, silver, and lead. As the government locks down the banks and the economy teeters, the question is whether being right about the collapse will be enough to survive it.

releases.title: Stumble by Fanis Michalakis
releases.summary: A seaside village is dancing to live jazz when a drone carrier blots out the sun with a 24-hour eviction notice from the Earth Central Bank. The villagers have three options: comply, fight, or take the Bank to a court run by bots that always rule for it. One young woman refuses to accept that the game is rigged.

releases.title: The Big Slash by DJ Bodden
releases.summary: You’re bagging your groceries when your payment is declined, and so is everyone else’s. Overnight, your money, your identity, your degree, even the lock on your door vanish with a dead chip in your palm. In a world where owning anything now means someone else’s permission, one ordinary man has to work out who he is when the keys to his life stop working.

releases.title: Yourself Myself E-self by Chris Griffiths
releases.summary: The world’s top scientists meet to plan how to squeeze every last watt from the planet, but by the fifth meeting everyone at the table is a digital avatar. Their flesh-and-blood selves are thousands of kilometres away, and that’s against protocol. Something has gone very wrong in the Meganet, and the glitches are getting creepier by the minute.

releases.title: Financial Fallout
releases.summary:
Currencies debased. 
Privacy under attack. 
Cash goes underground. 
The crushing weight of debt. 
We were never prepared. 

Welcome to a system designed to keep us poor. The harder we work, the less we gain.
And as we struggle, the noose only tightens. 
And then, when we have nothing left to lose, we turn on those who rigged the game. 
We stand and fight. 

These 21 stories portray unfortunate yet brilliant heroes fighting the powers that triggered financial fallout. Money is broken, but hope is not lost.

***

DM for access to access to a Underworld, a bonus story by Max Hillebrand.

releases.title: The Journal's Alchemists
releases.summary: In a dimly lit study adorned with ancient tomes and peculiar artifacts, a figure hunched over a weathered desk, immersed in the calculations that consumed his thoughts. Pierre de Fermat, a man of mathematical brilliance, was in a race against time, though he hardly recognized it as such. The room was permeated with the scent of aged parchment and the weight of centuries-old knowledge. The candlelight cast eerie shadows across Pierre’s furrowed brow as he delved into a labyrinth of equations. I hadn’t spoken to her in over eighteen months, so a 2 AM call from the perennial fun-sponge could only mean bad news.
“Hi, Corinne. What’s the emergency?” I mumbled, somewhere between still drunk and hungover.

Disembarking, they gazed, wide-eyed like children, upon the colossal construction works. releases.title: Who Let the Bitcoin Dogs Out?
releases.summary:
The engine revs.
“I can’t believe we were able to find an American Mustang in this French countryside.” John celebrates by punching the air. “I am ripping down these narrow roads.”
“Bloody hell. Slow down!” Lily begs as her oversized diamond dangle earrings sway side to side. “You’ve got nothing to prove, John. Big man in your Yankee ten-gallon hat. Let’s just get there safely.”
John slows to give her a smoldering look and charm her with his southern drawl, “Aww, my sweet British compatriot, you care about me.”

releases.title: Eye in the Sky
releases.summary:
“We should have gone there instead,” Simon Derwall complained.
His wife was furiously scrubbing a gigantic saucepan with a sponge, and the objection stopped her in her tracks. A deadly silence filled the air. She had explained this to him several times already.
“The king’s visit brings eyes with it. Why are we compromising our OPSEC like this?” Simon continued.
Elena Negrón sighed and replied, “Father cannot travel, remember.”

They’d interrupted his shopping in the middle of this chaos. He kept his eyes on the bike and his mind on finding his groceries when he got back to the store.

releases.title: The Fable of the Tyrant Alchemist

In a kingdom once resplendent with bountiful markets and sky-reaching monuments, it was the first failed harvest that marked the end of affluence and the beginning of collapse.

releases.title: The Bitcoin Overlay
releases.summary:
No one knows exactly when the Great Schism began. Many claim that it never occurred — a mere figment of fevered imaginations. But for the outliers, the divide is an inescapable actuality. Some fled to far-off lands like Mexico or Sub-Saharan Africa seeking refuge, while others were completely cast out of society, left to fend for themselves in the fringes. And then there is me, the bridge between the two worlds.

There was an undulant blue blur to his world, like when he used to swim laps in his infinity pool on his Texan ranch. That had cost him a few bitcoins, but nothing like the fortune he’d paid to Cyrogen Futures. His nostrils tingled with an antiseptic chemical odor, like those from the many medical labs he funded. releases.summary:
When my father died, an entire ecosystem system of beneficiaries withered. Moussa Ag El Khir funded scholarships and community projects, paying thousands of dinars monthly to stop the oasis town of In Salah from burning up. The few families we knew operating outside the oil-field economy would be forced to flee to the Mediterranean coast, along with just about every other Berber.

releases.summary:
“Welcome to Bob’s free mining colony! You may still be experiencing the side effects of wormhole travel, but soon, your new life as an off-world miner will—”
The speaker coughed and died off, leaving the overly enthusiastic welcome unfinished. Johanna didn’t mind, as every word burrowed into her brain like a gimlet.

releases.title: Bitter Fly
releases.summary: He was instantly met by the wind when he stepped outside. A cold breeze climbed up Belmer Street, carrying dust, salt, and the scent of the sea. Adjusting his coat, Croissal crossed the street and descended into the subway. His discussion with Lady Lowry lasted longer than he had planned, and he was late for his next appointment. He should have cancelled this meeting with Lowry. Dealing with fretful wives and cheating husbands was part of the job — some months, a substantial part of the job — but, at the end of the day, all cases looked the same. releases.title: The Construct
releases.summary: Vincent trudged forward, burdened by his luggage as if weighed down by the desolate land’s very fabric. The final leg of the road writhed like a serpent, its ashen skin devoid of the comforting touch of asphalt. The ominous gloom swallowed the remnants of daylight, leaving him to navigate through a twilight realm of unease. “Remember the twelve words, Vincent,” he muttered before soldiering on. “This is the last contract. Just a few more days, then poof! No more meetings, no more deadlines, no more paperwork. After this, I’ll finally be free.”

releases.title: Lowery Station Terminal
releases.summary:
She leaned against the column nearest my couch in the Lowery Station launch bay and pinned me with a raised eyebrow. “Hi there, sailor,” she said. Her hair was slicked to one side, traces of star-burst colors washing through in a faded array of one-time glamour. Her clothing matched her hair’s old and defeated approach to fashion consciousness. She had the look of a late teen or early twenty-something.

I closed my copy of The Generational Standard and folded my hands on the book. Looking up, I asked, “Can I help you?”

releases.title: The Noderoid Saga: Dreamers
releases.summary: Tick, tock, next block — the incessant rhythm of my existence persists like Chinese water torture. I am a noderoid, a half-flesh, half-machine creature harnessed to propagate and store the timechain. My life is a ceaseless cycle of handling and relaying bitcoin data. Approximately every ten minutes, a binary flash sears through my circuits. It is the price I pay for my existence.

releases.title: Behemoth
releases.summary: The massive ship had just docked their home, Steadfast #2, and Flint Molvesper was ready to board. Wow, what a beast! he thought, as he ran towards the airlock. Normally, you could see deep space all around the docking bay. You could see none of it now. Flint had never seen anything like it.

releases.title: 21 Futures: Tales from the Timechain
releases.summary:
Welcome to the world's first bitcoin fiction anthology.

Noderoid cyborgs, hidden treasure in the Sahara, and a new world order in Panama.

In these twenty-one stories, some of bitcoin's brightest minds outline how the new era of sound money could affect humanity.

Including stories from Knut Svanholm, Ioni Appelberg, and Niko Laamanen.

REVIEW FROM BITCOIN MAGAZINE:
"Before the first best-selling bitcoin novel hits shelves, before the first bitcoin blockbuster opens at your local theater—you will want to read this book." Eric Bies.
